title: Spatial join + rates
query: zones.geojson holds 9 zones with a population field, and incidents.csv holds incident locations (lat/lon). Count the incidents in each zone and compute the rate per 1,000 residents. Which zone has the highest rate, and what is it?

answer:
Based on the spatial analysis performed, I joined the 256 incidents to the 9 zones (251 matched, 5 fell outside all zones) and computed the rate per 1,000 residents for each zone.

**The zone with the highest rate is Z2, at 22.89 incidents per 1,000 residents.**

Z2 has 19 incidents in a population of just 830 — a small population drives its rate far above the others. The next-highest is Z5 at 8.92 per 1,000.

### Full table (sorted by rate)

| Zone | Population | Incidents | Rate per 1,000 |
|------|-----------:|----------:|---------------:|
| **Z2** | 830 | 19 | **22.89** |
| Z5 | 7,400 | 66 | 8.92 |
| Z1 | 5,200 | 41 | 7.88 |
| Z4 | 2,600 | 18 | 6.92 |
| Z6 | 3,900 | 25 | 6.41 |
| Z8 | 6,100 | 37 | 6.07 |
| Z7 | 1,500 | 9 | 6.00 |
| Z3 | 4,100 | 22 | 5.37 |
| Z9 | 2,800 | 14 | 5.00 |

- **Interactive choropleth** of incidents per zone (on your map): [incidents_per_zone.geojson](https://agent/files/file_eafe7a63fa9c/download)
- **Results table CSV** (downloadable): [incident_rates_per_zone.csv](https://agent/files/file_c4553bb1bac0/download)

Note: 5 of the 256 incidents fell outside all zone polygons and were excluded from the counts.
